io.github.captainssingapura-hue.homing.js:homing-workspace-shell 0.5.4 发布, Universal workspace chrome substrate — the orchestrator and its
        sub-classes that every WorkspaceShell-derived AppModule shares.

        Born from a refactor: prior to this module, the entire workspace
        boot sequence (WorkspaceLayout mount, MTP wiring, picker plumbing,
        persistence attach, identity resolution, event-log + replay,
        checkpoint store, Web Lock + read-only fence) lived as ~2,100 lines
        of JS-as-Java-string-literals inside per-workspace chrome widgets
        (e.g. AnimalsPlaygroundChrome.bodyJs() in homing-demo). This
        module promotes that mass into proper ES modules — one class per
        responsibility, each independently testable.

        Doctrines made concrete:

        - Modest File Size: every class sits comfortably under the cap.
        - Generated and Hand-Written Live Apart: JS lives in .js files,
          not Java string-literal lists.
        - Functional Objects: each JS class has explicit state, pure
          behaviour, inspect() output (extended from the Java doctrine).
        - Diligent Secretaries: every component is testable in isolation
          via the GraalVM harness without a DOM.

        Position in the dep graph: sits above homing-workspace-persistence
        (the highest workspace utility module) so it can compose every
        substrate piece below.

io.github.captainssingapura-hue.homing.js:homing-workspace-codecs 0.5.4 发布, Generated JS codecs for the workspace's typed records. Doctrine —
        "Generated and Hand-Written Live Apart": this module's
        src/main/resources is empty; all served JS is produced by
        WorkspaceCodecGen.main() into target/classes during the
        generate-resources phase via the Maven exec plugin.

        The manifest of records-to-be-codeced is declared in
        WorkspaceStateCodecsManifest as a typed List of
        ObjectDefinition<?> instances. The Java DomModule
        (WorkspaceStateCodecsModule) declares the matching Exportable._Class
        records so the framework's EsModuleWriter can wire imports across
        the JS module boundary.

        Cycle A — foundation slice. Manifest contains PaneId only; subsequent
        cycles expand to all 18 workspace records and add specialised
        codegens for sealed sums, enums, collections, Optionals, and Instant.

io.github.captainssingapura-hue.homing.js:homing-codec 0.5.4 发布, Meta-Function ontology — the higher-level interface layer that names
        the typed objects involved in moving data across language seams via
        generated code rather than runtime reflection.

        Four ontology objects:

        1. ObjectDefinition<T> — typed source-of-truth
        2. TransformationFunctions<T, W> — pure encode/decode pair
        3. FunctionsCodeGen — produces source code of TransformationFunctions
        4. DefinitionCodeGen — translates ObjectDefinition across languages

        Pure-interface module — no implementations. Concrete codecs live
        with their Value Objects in the modules that own those records
        (Names Are Types in action: each Object Definition's codec is
        co-located with the Object Definition itself).

        Doctrinal anchor: CodeGen as Functions. Hand-written, automated,
        and AI-assisted implementations all conform to the same interface;
        provenance is invisible at the contract boundary.

        Deferred: a Java-side JSON parser (for the day data flows back
        from JS to Java). Not needed yet — only Java→JS direction is in
        scope for the early consumers.

        2. TransformationFunctions<T, W> — pure encode/decode pair
        3. FunctionsCodeGen — produces source code of TransformationFunctions
        4. DefinitionCodeGen — translates ObjectDefinition across languages

        Pure-interface module — no implementations. Concrete codecs live
        with their Value Objects in the modules that own those records
        (Names Are Types in action: each Object Definition's codec is
        co-located with the Object Definition itself).

        Doctrinal anchor: CodeGen as Functions. Hand-written, automated,
        and AI-assisted implementations all conform to the same interface;
        provenance is invisible at the contract boundary.

        Deferred: a Java-side JSON parser (for the day data flows back
        from JS to Java). Not needed yet — only Java→JS direction is in
        scope for the early consumers.

io.github.captainssingapura-hue.homing.js:homing-rigid-tree 0.5.4 发布, The normalized rigid tree — RFC 0040. A dedicated, substrate-free
        module holding only the definition and arithmetic of a leveled
        rigid tree: pure values and functions, zero framework dependencies.

        Borrows DomOpsParty's leveled-types pattern, capped at 18 levels
        (L0..L18) to retain rigidity. Contents:
        - TreeLevel              — sealed sum L0..L18 + atDepth/shifted/above
        - TreeNode<L>       — typed leveled node contract
        - NormalizedNode         — the one canonical node every source maps to
        - Dimension / DimensionKey / DimensionValue + the bundled keys/values
        - RigidTrees.shift(...)  — graft: a pure recursive level shift
        - TreeNormalizer<SPEC> — the per-source-encoding seam

        Everything else (TreeNodeJsonWriter serialization in
        homing-tree-views, the studio-base normalizers, the JS TreeRenderer)
        depends ON this module — never the reverse. Substrate doctrine made
        physical: the tree value algebra cannot pick up serialization,
        rendering, or any source encoding.

io.github.captainssingapura-hue.homing.js:homing-tree-views 0.5.4 发布, Rigid tree substrate — typed leveled TreeNode value objects + a
        canonical JSON serialiser that becomes the universal contract for
        rendering any tree-shaped artifact on JS without a single line of
        per-tree-kind JS code.

        Borrows DomOpsParty's leveled-types pattern: TreeLevel is a sealed
        sum (L0..L8); TreeNode<L extends TreeLevel> is parameterised on
        its depth. Per-tree-kind adapter records (in studio-base and
        downstream modules) map native shapes (catalogues, ComposedDoc
        segments, future tree-shaped doc kinds) to TreeNode<L> — a
        thin String-to-typed-wrapping boundary.

        Substrate vocabulary:
        - Dimension(key, value)      — typed metadata pair
        - DimensionKey               — sealed; small substrate vocabulary
        - DimensionValue             — non-sealed; extension point
        - DisplayLabel / LevelDepth  — bundled DimensionKey constants
        - NameValue / DepthValue     — bundled DimensionValue records
        - TreeNodeJsonWriter         — canonical JSON serialiser

        Doctrinal anchors: Names Are Types (no raw strings on the contract
        surface), Make It Impossible Not Forbidden (level type enforces
        per-depth shape), One Stone Two Birds (substrate consolidation +
        future pivot/grid/outline transforms compound on the same shape).

io.github.captainssingapura-hue.homing.js:homing-studio-starter 0.5.4 发布, Batteries-included entry point for downstream studios (RFC 0040). The
        workspace stack (homing-workspace / -shell / -studio-workspace) is a
        strict downstream of homing-studio-base, so the "studio + workspace
        out of the box" wiring cannot live in studio-base itself (it would
        close a dependency cycle). This module sits ABOVE the whole stack and
        ties it together:

        - StudioStarterFixtures — a Fixtures that IS DefaultFixtures plus the
          Studio Workspace pre-wired: GenericWorkspace served, StudioWorkspaceSpec
          registered, and GET /catalogue-tree rooted at the studio forest.

        A downstream studio depends on THIS module only, constructs
        `new StudioStarterFixtures<>(umbrella)` instead of
        `new DefaultFixtures<>(umbrella)`, and the catalogue Navigator,
        tree feed, and leveled Open all light up with no per-studio wiring.

        Doctrinal anchor: A Good Design Doesn't Pick Up Its Substrate — the
        starter is the one place the application-assembly defaults are
        composed; nothing below it knows the workspace exists.

        classes). Provides:

        - EcmaDefinitionCodeGen — emits a JS class declaration mirroring a
          Java record (or sealed-of-records) ObjectDefinition.
        - EcmaFunctionsCodeGen — emits a JS TransformationFunctions
          implementation (transformTo / transformFrom) for the same.

        Stateless FunctionalObject implementations. The "Codegen as
        Functions" doctrine — same code runs at build time (Maven exec
        plugin) and could run at request time if a downstream consumer
        ever wants runtime generation.

        Pure-Java module; produces JS source as String values. The build-
        time invocation lives in the consumer module (e.g.,
        homing-workspace-codecs), not here.

io.github.captainssingapura-hue.homing.js:homing-ssjs-test-fixtures 0.5.4 发布, Test fixtures for pure-JavaScript code authored under the homing
        ssjs (server-side-JS) substrate.

        Vends a GraalVM-Polyglot-backed JUnit harness so any pure JS module
        — Secretaries (RFC 0028), client-side reducers, validators,
        serialisation helpers — can be unit-tested on the JVM against a real
        ECMAScript runtime, without spinning up a browser or transpiling.

        The harness is split into two layers:

          - JsModuleTestBase — generic. Boots a JS context, loads a module
            from the classpath, looks up named exports, ships an envelope()
            helper that marshals Java Maps into native JS objects via
            ProxyObject, and tears the context down on @AfterEach.

          - SecretaryTestBase — Diligent-Secretaries-doctrine layer. Adds
            the Step contract — initial(), dispatch(state, env) — and terse
            assertions over { newState, actions }.

        Dependencies (GraalVM Polyglot + js-community) are exposed at
        compile scope intentionally: this module IS test fixtures, so a
        downstream test module pulling it in (typically at test scope from
        its own pom) automatically gets a working runtime with no further
        config.

        Public downstream projects can depend on this module identically to
        any homing artifact; the test-fixtures naming makes the intent
        legible at the dependency-graph level (vs. opaque test-jar
        classifiers, which the dependency-as-test-jar refactor explicitly
        replaced).

items.title:
io.github.captainssingapura-hue.homing.js:homing-workspace 0.5.4 发布, RFC 0025 — Workspace + Dynamic Widget Management. A strict downstream
        of homing-studio-base providing the workspace shell pattern: a
        per-page registry of WorkspaceWidget types, a controller that
        dynamically loads modules on user pick, a picker UI, and the
        WorkspaceShell AppModule base that ties it together.

        Studios that don't need workspace capabilities (catalogue browsers,
        doc readers, single-widget viewers) leave this dependency off and pay
        nothing for the machinery. Studios that want workspace add this dep.

        The WorkspaceWidget contract is distinct from RFC 0024's Widget — see
        the Rfc0025Ext1Doc for the design and the rationale. Both contracts
        coexist; a WorkspaceWidget can be hosted in a non-workspace context
        by wrapping it in a degenerate mini-workspace (one widget, no picker,
        no layout management).

items.title:
io.github.captainssingapura-hue.homing.js:homing-studio-workspace 0.5.4 发布, The Studio Workspace — a reusable, spec-driven workspace for browsing
        a studio's catalogues inside the V2 workspace shell. Composes existing
        substrate pieces with zero new chrome JS:

        - TreeWidget          — a WorkspaceWidget that fetches a catalogue
                                 subtree as canonical TreeNode JSON and renders
                                 it with the generic TreeRenderer (homing-core-js).
        - CatalogueTreeGetAction — GET /catalogue-tree?id=<slug> — serializes
                                 a Catalogue subtree via CatalogueTreeAdapter +
                                 TreeNodeJsonWriter. Wired downstream via
                                 Fixtures.harnessGetActions() with the studio's
                                 root catalogue.
        - StudioWorkspaceSpec — a WorkspaceSpec (kind "studio") that pins the
                                 TreeWidget; mounted by GenericWorkspace at
                                 ?app=genericWorkspace&ws_kind=studio.

        First widget is the tree view; a studio-navigation Party (tree
        selection -> open doc in a tab) lands in a follow-up.

        Doctrinal anchors: A Good Design Doesn't Pick Up Its Substrate (the
        spec declares only what's studio-specific), Make It Impossible Not
        Forbidden (no hand-written chrome JS — only the declarative surface).

items.title:
io.evitadb:evita_root 2026.1.19 发布, Evita is a specialized database with easy-to-use API for e-commerce systems. Purpose of this research is
		creating fast and scalable engine that handles all complex tasks that e-commerce systems has to deal with on
		daily basis.

		Evita should operate as a fast secondary lookup / search index used by application frontends. We aim for order
		of magnitude better latency (10x faster or better) for common e-commerce tasks than other solutions based on SQL
		or NoSQL databases on the same hardware specification. Evita should not be used for storing and handling primary
		data, and we don't aim for ACID properties nor data corruption guarantees. Evita "index" must be treated
		as something that could be dropped any time and built up from scratch easily again.
